generationRecipe: A ruled ground for a short table of results: a returns board or a printed canvass sheet, the thing results were read off before there was a screen. Counted and official rather than celebratory.

It must hold THREE TO FIVE rows without distortion or a visible seam. Two was the only case until 2026-09-22, when the single hardcoded opponent was replaced with a field of two to four; measured in the browser the same day, Chicago returned five candidates and Galena five.
A sentence sits above the rows, one to two lines, naming who won.
No words, numerals or lettering of any kind in the artwork. Every name and every share is generated for that contest.
No party marks, emblems or colours. The parties in this game are real organizations and their branding is not ours to draw.
The same treatment is used whether the player won or lost, so nothing in it may read as a trophy or as a defeat. The game's own position is that a lost election leaves the life running.
acceptanceCriteria: Reads at a glance as the end of something, distinct from the ordinary notes above it on the same panel.
Holds three, four and five rows equally well; a delivery that only composes at two candidates is wrong.
Contains no text, numerals or lettering. A delivery with any lettering in it is wrong however good it looks.
Carries no party emblem, colour coding or anything that could be read as one.
Reads the same for a win and for a loss.
Does not reduce the contrast of the names and percentages sitting on it.
